summary: Blob bytes move out of the main store into their own file, <store>.blobs.<ext> beside it, three days after a member first runs this build ([store] blob_move_after). The blobs table keeps every row with its hash and size; an hourly paced pass copies rows' bytes into the blob file, lets a checkpoint of the blob file (off the writer) put them on disk, then empties those rows and gives the pages back. Readers take a blob's bytes from either place. On a copy of a real 56.7 GB member (208,285 blobs, 1.87 GB of bytes), the main file shrank to 54.8 GB: the blobs table went from 2.01 GB to 0.44 GB (emptied rows leave sparse pages behind), and the blob file holds 2.03 GB. Disk use overall is about the same; what shrinks is the file every query reads.

replay.detail: Claims, envelopes and replication are unchanged: a blob's bytes still travel in the envelope that names it, and where a member keeps them is local.

schema.detail: A second SQLite file, the blob file, attached to every connection as blob_file, with blobs(hash, bytes, size), WAL and incremental auto-vacuum. Three meta keys: blob_file_since, blob_file_moved_through and blob_file_fenced_from. The first emptied row raises the store's user_version to 25. blobs leaves the projection digest (projection version blobs 2).

rules.detail: The projection digest no longer covers blobs. A blob is bound by the hash in each claim that names it, and the claim digests compare those. Peers of either version compare blobs only when both report projection version 2, so mixed versions read no divergence.

compatibility.detail: Mixed versions in both directions: nothing on the wire changes, and blobs leave the projection digest by per-table version. A previous release refuses the [store] section: set blob_move_after only after upgrading, and remove it before rolling back.

downtime.detail: No migration at start. The move runs in the background, each step one writer hold (a copy, or an emptying of rows whose copies a checkpoint has made durable) of about 40 ms, with a rest of four times the hold, and gives free pages back 128 at a time. Measured on that copy with builds running, 3,616 holds: p50 1.2 ms, p99 44.5 ms, max 186 ms, 0.08% over 100 ms; the smallest ordinary write in the same run p50 1.2 ms, p99 14.5 ms, max 1.86 s, 0.25% over 100 ms. Free-page steps: p50 5.2 ms, p99 56 ms, max 140 ms. The first open of this build reseeds the projection digest once (blobs left it); on that copy it opened in 16 s.

manual.detail: To roll back after the move started, stop the daemon and run `fractal store restore-blob-bytes --store <path>` first. [store] blob_move_after (default 3d) lengthens the window before any byte moves.

recovery.detail: Within three days of upgrading (blob_move_after), a rollback to the previous release works as before: no byte has moved. After that, the store is at user_version 25, which the previous release refuses to open rather than serve empty blobs. `fractal store restore-blob-bytes` copies every byte back and lowers it to what it was. Crash safety: a row is emptied only after a checkpoint of the blob file has put its copy on disk. A copy of the store needs its blob file beside it: checkpoint proof copies take it; an operator's hand-made copy must too. Offline backups stream envelope payloads, which still carry the bytes.
